# BDD Harness

**The registry drives the suite, and the tests are committed artefacts of it.** `docs/scenarios.yaml` says what the engine must do; `build tests` renders one Go test per scenario into the file its `path:` names; `pkg/testkit/bddgo` runs it. No feature files. A scenario with an unbound step FAILS — never skipped, never silently absent. See `docs/scenarios.yaml` for the scenario shape (real examples, every entry).

**Every test file under `tests/*/` beginning `// Code generated` is written by `true-bdd build tests --fix` and nothing else** — deterministic codegen: the same registry always renders the same bytes, which is what lets `build tests` verify by regenerate-and-compare. A stale file is a startup refusal naming the regeneration command. The AI turn survives only where judgement is needed: authoring step definitions.

Generated tests state their steps literally, and `Done()` compares them against the registry entry before running any — a disagreement stops the scenario with both sides printed. The registry supplies what is not behaviour: description, `service:`, `timeout:`.

**`path:` is required on every scenario, never defaulted.** Several scenarios may share one file (emitted in id order — grouping is editorial). The generator refuses a `path:` outside `tests/<service>/` — the mirror of `services/<service>/`, and the directory it derives the package clause and scenarios import from — one not ending `_test.go`, one inside `steps/`, and two ids rendering one Go name. A path shared across services is now unreachable rather than refused: the directory decides the service.

**Hand-written guards** (`tests/*/coverage_test.go`) keep the generated set honest — hand-written so the generator cannot silence them by regenerating: `TestScenarioCoverage` (every scenario ↔ exactly one generated test, in the named file), `TestFixtureTreesArePaired` and `TestFixtureTemplateOverlays`. None brings a harness up; all answer in under a second. **Step coverage is not a test any more** — the engine reads `steps/` itself, so an unbound step surfaces when `build steps` runs and nowhere else. bddgo's own refusals: a service the architecture does not declare, a step matched by two definitions, a generated test naming a scenario the registry no longer holds, a `Done()` never called.

**Step prefixes** — two hand a step to a model, each legal in exactly one block; the wrong block is a refusal, not a reinterpretation:

| prefix | legal in | means | needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `llm:` | given/when | a model performs the step, one agent turn at its position | `bddgo.Actor` |
| `judge:` | then | a model rules on the clause — collected, then ONE call after every other step passed | `bddgo.Judgeable` |

Use `judge:` only for what no comparison can settle (two wordings meaning the same thing). The true-bdd state implements only `Judgeable`; `Actor` is unimplemented — deliberate forward work.

**Fixtures**: each true-bdd scenario drives a tree at `tests/true-bdd/fixtures/<name>/` — `input/` (the designed host-project content) and `cassettes/` (one dir per AI call plus `golden.json`). **There is no manifest** — what the run does comes from the scenario; its Given step names the tree. A tree no scenario names fails the whole run. Three optional files at the fixture ROOT, read **by content** rather than executed by path: `prep.sh` (runs after the input overlay, before the pre-run snapshot; non-zero aborts), `teardown.sh` (at SCENARIO end — after both snapshots AND after every Then step, whatever the verdict; never masks it. Late deliberately: a Then step that re-runs the host suite needs the stack the run left standing. A fixture that starts a server takes its port, and a compose stack its project name, from its own run dir's path, never a fixed one: with a fixed port a parallel run's server is reused or torn down, and the walk finds no failure to fix), `checklist-prompts.yaml` (narrows the checklist walk, keyed by stem; present-but-empty is refused). The scenario still names all three as Given steps; the step definitions verify the tree establishes them.

**Offline replay's network need:** `build-code-spec-005-matched-scenario-embedded` declares `github.com/ondatra-ai/true-bdd/pkg@v0.0.0-20261027174914-58543b8e324b` as a testing library. The engine downloads it and its build graph before the writer even in services replay. A cold module cache therefore needs the Go proxy once; warm that graph first for a fully disconnected replay. AI requests themselves stay offline and free.

**Record/replay**: `pkg/testkit/aiproxy` is one binary installed as `claude`/`codex` in a shim dir prepended to the subprocess PATH — **one dir per CALLER**, because the shim reads its whole configuration from flat env vars, so separate dirs are the only way the engine can replay while the judge records. A recording shim skips EVERY dir in `TRUE_BDD_AIPROXY_KNOWN_SHIMS` when hunting the genuine CLI, not just its own: with two shims on PATH, skipping only its own finds the other and execs it, which recurses. A `live` caller actively SCRUBS the other caller's shim dir and the four `TRUE_BDD_AIPROXY_*` vars from the spawn it controls — inheritance is the default, and a caller that keeps another's shim has its turns answered from the wrong shelf, consuming that shelf's cursor on the way. A cassette stores argv, stdin, output streams, exit code, and fs-diff, with volatile paths normalized (`{{CWD}}`, `{{RUN_DIR}}`, `{{HOME}}`, `{{GOROOT}}`) in paths, contents AND stdout. The shim normalizes the installed GOROOT in every request and recorded stream, including Go diagnostics embedded in prompts, and restores the replaying toolchain root on replay. Whole-path boundaries preserve sibling paths. New validation recordings omit engine-owned per-run artifacts before snapshot traversal to avoid concurrent staging renames and cross-turn effects; codex keeps its own -o answer file. Existing cassettes remain untouched. New recordings carrying Go test frame durations set normalize_go_durations in their cassette metadata and canonicalize only those elapsed values to 0.00s in request argv/stdin; failure text stays whole. Replay applies that rule only when declared by the cassette, so legacy recordings retain their exact hash contract. Replay atomically claims an unconsumed cassette by normalized request hash per binary, applying each cassette's declared Go-duration normalization. Identical requests consume their matching cassettes in recorded-number order; no metadata or existing recording changes. A consumed-name receipt replaces the replay cursor for the cassette census. All mismatch = loud "stale cassette" failure, **exit 86**, never a silent fall-through — applies the fs-diff, and lingers until the engine closes stdin. **Cassettes are sanitized before writing** (the agent CLI's system/init inventory dropped, home rewritten, private Go telemetry counter basenames replaced); the `Recordings` gate (`scripts/gates/recordings.go`) re-checks committed recordings — a hit means fix the shim and re-record, **never hand-edit a cassette**.

**Engine-owned IO (#224):** `engine-io-001` through `engine-io-010` pin parent-directory hold contention, its ten-second timeout and shared readers, atomic replacement with old modes and stale staging symlinks, exact streams, large Claude events, usage/denial log keys, Go's Git-hook environment scrubbing, cancellation of both CLIs' descendants, and Claude's child environment. The explicit observed-Claude Given puts a fixture-only `claude-only/` launcher before the proxy in every mode; the real deterministic stand-in checks poisoned parent/session flags, role and advisor settings, and the writer's stripped flags, timeouts and isolation switches at spawn. It never calls a model and records no Claude cassette. Codex stays behind the existing lifecycle-observing proxy. Cancellation fixtures likewise run deterministic CLIs directly in every mode. Hold and atomic-write launch barriers run after the pre-run snapshot. Blocked-read probes also require the engine PID to remain alive before unlocking, so a blocked post-run harness snapshot cannot satisfy them. Every fixture is still recorded through the declared record command; these ten Scenarios cost $0. No test-library change is needed.

**Generated writer configuration (ADR-0026):** the request hash covers normalized argv and stdin, not the contents of files referenced by argv or environment. In particular, codex's generated CODEX_HOME/config.toml and Claude's --settings file are not request inputs to the hash. Codex homes are deliberately excluded from snapshots before traversal, so replay and goldens alone cannot detect a malformed permission profile. `writer-config-001-codex` and `writer-config-002-claude` close this gap with the existing `every file matching … matches …` step: after a controlled `build code --fix`, anchored patterns inspect the engine-generated configuration directly in every mode. The every-file step substitutes `{{CWD}}` with the symlink-resolved run root and `{{GOROOT}}`/`{{GOMODCACHE}}` with `go env -json` roots. Paths are escaped as JSON string contents in .json files and TOML basic string contents in .toml files, then regex-escaped; other files use raw paths before regex escaping. `{{ENGINE}}` substitutes the engine executable (invoked or symlink-resolved path), also escaping internal shell single quotes before JSON escaping for the hook. The hook pattern elides only its run basename. The assertions retain table names, keys, types, entry order and deny rules. Optional installed codex runtime read grants and :minimal comments are tolerated. No credentials are opened. These Scenarios pin form, while live sandbox probes establish the CLIs' enforcement; neither substitutes for the other. Existing cassette requests and recordings stay unchanged.

**Live-only behaviour must have a Scenario pin (ADR-0026, #210):** a rebuild drops behaviour that only a live CLI needs unless a Scenario observes it independently of replayed effects. `writer-lifecycle-001-success`, `writer-lifecycle-002-failure` and `engine-io-003-events` opt into fixture-controlled authentication and external CLI stand-ins. Only these fixtures' declared dummy `auth/auth.json` and generated dummy copies may be inspected; never open real credentials. Before record or replay effects, the codex shim checks the exact copy, 0600 file, 0700 generated home, absence of other inherited home files, protected home location and deny entry, empty provisioned edit root, and private shell scratch. It writes a non-secret per-run receipt under snapshot-filtered `tmp/aiproxy-state/`, never into a cassette; the Then requires it and checks auth removal after success or exit 7. Exact JSONL sentinel comparison pins stdout-only event archival; stderr must reach the combined transcript. `writer-config-001-codex` pins the complete shell policy. Native sandbox enforcement still needs the installed-CLI calibration described by ADR-0021/0024; a replay cannot establish an OS sandbox's enforcement. New live-only claims need a Scenario or an explicit explanation of that limit. These fixtures' `cli/claude` and `cli/codex` are deterministic external boundary stand-ins selected behind the shim, so recording with dummy authentication makes no model calls. In live mode only these opt-in fixtures use a services observing pass-through shim and the same stand-ins. Normal live turns remain unmediated. Requests still hash only argv/stdin, and all existing recordings remain byte-identical.

**Grading, three levels, each owning what the others cannot say**: (1) the scenario's Then steps — every mechanical assertion (exit code, stdout, file diff, AI-turn counts) **and any suite the scenario re-runs itself**, every mode; (2) the recording, replay only — `golden.json` byte-compare, every cassette consumed (`runner.CheckCassettesConsumed`), request hash per call; (3) the judge — the `judge:` clauses, **every mode**, one verdict per clause as schema-enforced JSON (`--json-schema`) on the pinned `engine.models.quick` model, in a tool-less headless turn through `pkg/cli/claude`; a malformed reply is an infrastructure error, never a scenario verdict. Under `tests:replay` that verdict is SERVED BACK from the fixture's own judge shelf rather than re-ruled, and a replayed verdict is not billed — the cassette carries the cost the recording spent once, and charging it again would report money no run spent. A fixture asked to replay a verdict it never recorded fails THAT fixture at its Given step, naming the command that records it; that failure is infrastructure, never `ErrJudgeRefused`, or `grade()`'s suppression would hide the golden mismatch beside it. **Cassettes belong to the When stage; Then is the same code path in every mode.** Levels 2 and 3 do not overlap and neither discharges the other: the golden and the census are WHEN-fidelity (the replay reproduced the recorded tree and consumed every turn), the judge grades the outcome's semantics, and both must hold. The judge prompt is generated by `runner.buildJudgeUserPrompt` — clauses rendered under a scope paragraph and one shared `## Tolerances` policy; nothing else feeds it. Noise dirs (`.git`, `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `test-results/`, `playwright-report/`) are excluded from both snapshots. Generated codex homes (credentials included) and codex shell/build scratch are skipped before both run and per-call snapshots walk them, so credentials and runtime-bin symlinks are never read or recorded; they never enter cassette fs-diffs. `tmp/` is excluded from the judge's diff outright (`runner.judgeGraded`) — the goldens already ignore it, no clause names it, and it carries the agent CLIs' own scratch, a 128KB SQLite db among it. The judge's diff is otherwise WHOLE: no per-file or total byte cap, since trimming it is what failed us-refine-verdicts-001-passing-story-saved-in-place on content it was never shown. **The judge is measurable under `services:replay,tests:live`**, and that is why that pairing exists: `JudgeRequest` is `(Cmd, Clauses, Diff)` and nothing else, and a green golden certifies that input is byte-identical run to run — so `judge_input_hash` (sha256 of the rendered user prompt, in `harness.json`) equal across two runs with different verdicts is the judge's own noise, and a differing hash is harness drift. A series is N separate `go test` invocations, never `-count=N`: `bootOnce` shares one session root and `prepareRunDir` wipes the fixture dir each iteration, leaving one surviving data point. Residual gap: scratch changes without an explicit Then assertion, stdout change or graded output file remain unchecked; the generated writer configurations have explicit Then assertions.

**Step-text conventions**: `and:`/`but:` are display-only sugar, interchangeable and unlimited (keyword excluded from the match text; convention: `but:` for a group's negative clause). Two path-argument families: the story steps (`the story "…"`, `… of the story "…"`) take a **glob that must resolve to exactly one file** — zero and two matches each fail; the diff/content steps (`the file "…" is created/modified/unchanged/matches`, `has exactly N lines`) take a **literal path**. Where a created file's name is unknowable: `exactly N file(s) matching "<glob>" is created`. Stdout and stderr patterns and regex tails run undelimited to end of line — several carry double quotes of their own. `{{CWD}}` in the When command stands for the run dir's absolute path, the token cassettes store it as (`engine-documents-001`). **`the shell command "<argv>" run in "<dir>" exits with code N`** re-runs a suite the scenario names, in a directory under the run's tmpdir, through `pkg/cli/spec` — the outcome check that a `build code` scenario means: the tests the fix loop was driving actually pass. Put it LAST among the mechanical Thens, since a re-run may append to files earlier clauses count (`build-code-run-004-fix-reruns-fixed-test`'s `suite-runs.log`), and prefer it over file-existence proxies — `build-code-run-005-playwright-fix-loop-converges` once failed a correct product over an optional `next.config.*` while its browser assertion was green.

**Claude writer hook**: the guard Scenarios run `true-bdd claude-guard --policy <file>` with the complete JSON tool payload on stdin. Given steps build file roots and exact replay forms; Then steps assert exit 0/2 and denial reasons. Symbolic links are planted during prep under snapshot-skipped `node_modules`.

**Tmpdir assembly**: repo layer first (tracked `true-bdd/` + `templates/`, so fixtures exercise the live templates), then the fixture's `input/` overlaid on top — fixture files win, so a fixture may ship a variant checklist or config. A file no overlay can take away (the repo's own `true-bdd/true-bdd.yaml`) a scenario drops with the Given `the project tree has no "<path>"`: the assembled run dir loses it before prep, and a path not there to drop, or leading out of the run dir, fails the run (`engine-entry-001`, `-003`). Snapshot after prep, before the run: the graded diff holds only what the run itself changed.

**Module boundaries:** the harness builds aiproxy from `pkg/` during bring-up, but defers the engine build from `services/true-bdd/` through `runner.LazyBinary` until a definition first needs it. Its result, including a missing-service error, is shared: each Scenario fails at its own calling step. The `-engine-bin` oracle is resolved at that same point. In a copy without VCS metadata, root discovery stops at the complete Specification and module rather than walking back into the original checkout. Fixture prep, engine execution, teardown and Then-command reruns force `GOWORK=off`; a fixture never inherits this checkout's workspace. Go fixtures require `github.com/ondatra-ai/true-bdd/pkg` and replace it with the checkout's `pkg/`, copying that module's sums.

**go.mod sentinels, two traps**: (1) a fixture input tree carrying `.go` files must carry a sentinel `go.mod` — run dirs live inside the repo module, and without a boundary the root `go test ./...`/lint compile the deliberately-failing tests past runs left there; (2) `tests/true-bdd/fixtures/go.mod` covers cassette `fsdiff/after/` trees, which record only what an AI turn *changed* and so carry no `go.mod` of their own. That sentinel is never materialised into a run dir (the runner overlays `<fixture>/input/`, not the fixture directory).

**Modes and gates**: a `//go:build bdd` tag hides the suite from default `GOWORK=off go test ./...` in each module. One scenario = one top-level test named from its key in CamelCase (the lineage key `scen-check-003-unknown-id-refused` gives `TestScenCheck003UnknownIdRefused`), so `-run` names a scenario; `steps.TestName` mirrors the engine's renderer for the record hints. `-mode` names a mode per CALLER — `services:` the engine under test, `tests:` the harness's own judge — and both are always named: there is no shorthand and no default, since a mode nobody typed is how a run bills real money believing it replays. An ABSENT `-mode` stays legal and is refused at `bootHarness`, not at the flag: the coverage guards pass none and bring no harness up. `requiredCLIs` gates per axis — a replaying services caller needs no CLI at all, and only a non-replaying `tests:` axis needs `claude`. Live/record skip per scenario when a needed CLI is missing; **replay skips for nothing**. **No gate RUNS a scenario**: the table carries `go vet -tags bdd ./...` in each repository module and the coverage guards, and nothing that boots a harness (`scripts/gates/table.go`). `services:replay,tests:replay` costs nothing and takes under a minute, so run it by hand before you push — a golden mismatch has no other alarm. One gate list, one runner: `ci.yml` calls `go run ./scripts/cmd/gates run` and names no gate of its own (`gates.TestCIDoesNotHandListGates` pins that). Gate failure kinds: exit 86 = stale cassette, re-record the affected fixtures; golden mismatch = the run produced different files than the recording — the regression signal, worth reading before re-recording. The gates run `TestScenarioCoverage`, `TestFixtureTreesArePaired` and `TestFixtureTemplateOverlays`; there is no step-coverage gate. Every step of every Registry Scenario binds, so `build tests` on this repo costs zero AI turns. `-engine-bin=<absolute path>` drives a prebuilt engine instead of the one the harness builds: `go run ./scripts/cmd/engine_coverage` hands in an engine built with `-cover`, replays the whole suite against it, and writes every block no Scenario reached to `tmp/engine-coverage.md`. The engine inherits the harness's environment, which is how `GOCOVERDIR` reaches every engine run.

**A scenario's CLI run is capped at 5 minutes unless its registry entry declares `timeout:`** (`scenarios.scenarioTimeout`). A walk over a multi-prompt checklist blows past that — a `scen check` walk of eight model cells takes about seven minutes — and the kill surfaces at the When step as `command timed out after 5m0s` (`shell.ErrTimeout`), the partial recording discarded. **Size the budget from the turn count** — the fixture's cassette-dir count is that number. Measured over a full record run (126 turns, 2026-08-30) a turn costs 53s with a 53s standard deviation, so `N x 53s + 3σ√N + 2m` rounded up to five minutes gives 15m at 5 turns, 20m at 7-10, 25m at 12. A cap that merely covers the expected total is a coin flip: us-refine-verdicts-001-passing-story-saved-in-place's twelve turns average about ten minutes against the 10m it used to declare, and it timed out.

`--fix` scenarios supply keystrokes via `the <role> answers "1" to every question` — a generous run of that answer, one line per question; surplus lines are harmless (EOF exits the CLI cleanly).

**Known, deliberate inconsistency:** the `us-refine-*` fixtures still ship the OLD `quality_gate.tests.{integration,e2e}` architecture shape, and the `us-refine` checklist still cites "the framework per service and per layer". Nothing parses those documents, so the cassettes stay valid — but do not read those fixtures as the current spec shape.

**Run dirs** — `tmp/test_run/<timestamp>/<fixture>/`: predictable, never auto-cleaned. `true-bdd-logs/` are recorder sidecars written from `t.Cleanup` (after both snapshots, never in the judge's diff): `harness.json` (verdict, cost, `judge_input_hash`; its presence means the fixture is final — the report server's cache key), `judge-{system,user,response}.txt`, `manifest.json` (what the run was held to as it resolved it). `tmp/true-bdd.log.json` is the engine's own slog, written during the run. At the session root: `session.json` (the `-mode` and planned fixtures, written before the first fixture), `harness.log.json` (the test process's slog), `.cassettes-staging/<fixture>/` (record-mode cassettes + golden, promoted into `fixtures/` only when the fixture passes; the judge's shelf stages at `<fixture>/judge/` inside it, so a run recording both publishes them in one rename, and a run recording only the judge merges that one directory rather than replacing the cassettes it replayed from).

Fixture template extensions preserve the shipped template prefix literally, including the codex/Claude completion conditional.

**Concurrent validation fixtures:** `scen-check-speed-001` and `-002` select deterministic Claude programs behind the recording proxy. A fixture launcher before it admits alpha then beta while recording, beta then alpha while replaying. A barrier requires both validation turns outstanding. Their deliberate override copies the shipped description-format and step-presence Q Prompts and appends a given-when-then D Prompt after them, sanctioned as overrideChecks to observe D-before-Q. Then steps read the engine log for D-before-Q, failed-D skipping, overlapping different Scenarios, sequential Q turns and serial applied menus alpha,beta followed by the explicit exit at gamma's menu; the reverse-order Then reads the proxy's consumed-name receipt. Both use the declared record command and cost $0.

**Concept link fixtures:** model-judgement Scenarios (`concept-link-*` and `concepts-fix-binding`) use the real CLIs and the model tiers shipped by `true-bdd init`, recorded through the declared record command. Only `concept-link-malformed`, `concept-link-missing-answer` and `concept-link-incomplete` select `input/cli/claude`, through the explicit Given `the link answer CLI is controlled for invalid replies`: the answer schema prevents a real model from supplying these invalid answers. No other concept-link fixture uses `input/cli/` or `link-case.json`. Engine Go tests at the request and walk seams pin required-key schemas, architecture-free link requests, sketches with embedded product meanings and service interface kinds without architecture read paths, and link-before-sketch ordering. Menu answers remain on stdin.
